- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.3 to +0.78 in sentiment) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.21 or below) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in price correction: model often lags 1–3 days behind true price movements, especially after sharp moves.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating long-term trend reversion toward historical mean.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early periods (first 5–7 days) and underestimate late periods (last 5–7 days) — adjust for asymmetric decay.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.5, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days; if sentiment < 0.3, increase forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 days.
